body:
I suggest removing the section [V51.4 OAuth Authorization Server](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x51-V51-OAuth2.md#v514-oauth-authorization-server).

The reasoning is, that an authorization is a very specific type of application. I think this is not in scope for the ASVS. When someone implements such a thing relevant standards must be consulted. 

However, there are some requirements in that section that concern the configuration of clients at the AS. I think those should be included as they are valid for all applications that also should fulfill the requirements in V51.2.

These requirements are in my opinion:
| # | Description | Level |
| :---: | :--- | :---: |
| **51.4.3** | [ADDED] Verify that, if the code grant is used, the authorization server mitigates authorization code interception attacks by requiring proof key for code exchange (PKCE). For authorization requests, the authorization server must require a valid 'code_challenge' value and must not accept 'code_challenge_method' value 'plain'. For a token request, it must require validation of the 'code_verifier' parameter. | 2 |
| **51.4.5** | [ADDED] Verify that for a given client, the authorization server only allows the usage of grants that this client needs to use. Note that the grants 'token' (Implicit flow) and 'password' (Resource Owner Password Credentials flow) must no longer be used. | 2 |
| **51.4.6** | [ADDED] Verify that the authorization server validates redirect URIs based on a client-specific allowlist of pre-registered URIs using exact string comparison. | 1 |

comments.body:
Hi @BenjaminHae  and thank you for reaching out.

We have went through the scoping - should we have OAuth and OIDC at all, how much we should have etc, and reached to the result we have.

Requirements in section V51.4 are all to be sure, that configuration for the OAuth client and communication between OAuth client and an authorization server is done securely. There is no requirement to dictate how someone needs to implement an authorization server.

An application (OAuth client) can not be secure on its own if the requirements in V51.4 are not satisfied.

To not have issues just hanging, I'll close this out based on arguments provided above - as we decided to cover OAuth and OIDC requirements, we need to have confidence that both sides of communication (OAuth client, Authorization Server) are doing their part correctly.
